messages:
marta: Heads-up — ran into a UX gap while reviewing console telemetry: we have ~6 different internal status tags for quota/fallback but the client-facing surface is a single 429 with generic text. This is making it hard for product to explain 'why' to customers.
ken: +1. Can you paste an example of the internal statuses? curious how distinct they are.
sasha: from infra side: we emit `quota_exhausted`, `burst_exceeded`, `reserved_capacity_spill`, `soft_throttle`, `hard_throttle`, and `route_blocked` depending on where the request dropped.
marta: exactly. Internally these are useful for routing + autoscale heuristics, but externally the SDK just sees 429 or 503 and panics. Product wants clearer guidance messages and retry semantics per-case.
devon: this is also hurting observability. Dashboards show spike of 429s but we can't partition by cause without joining logs -> tedious. Proposal: include a compact header + telemetry tag that maps to a public-facing enum.
priya: idea: send `X-Redwood-Status: quota.burst` and `X-Redwood-Retry-After: 30` when applicable. And on telemetry emit `client.error.v2` with attrs `reason=quota.burst, route=best-effort, variant=quantized`.
zack: small caution: headers leak internal signal if named badly. Keep names generic and documented. maybe `X-RW-Error` or `X-Redwood-Info`.
marta: agreed. Naming threshold: public but stable. Also we should not expose capacity sizes or tier names.
ken: for the client message copy, product suggested three tiers: "soft limit — try again soon", "reserved limit — contact sales for more throughput", "transient/try-again — retry with backoff". Thoughts?
sasha: mapping: soft_throttle -> soft limit message + `Retry-After`; reserved_capacity_spill -> reserved limit + no auto-retry; hard_throttle/route_blocked -> terminal with link to docs; quota_exhausted -> reserved message if over plan.
devon: and for SDKs we can surface structured error object: `type: "quota", subtype: "burst", retry: 30, public_code: "quota_burst"` so apps can programmatically handle without relying on headers.
priya: console work: add a split view on the 429 dashboard that shows counts by `public_code` and a small guidance card per code with suggested mitigation (backoff, contact sales, switch to dedicated capacity).
zack: telemetry naming: prefer `rw.client.error` metric + tag `public_code` so queries are simple. Avoid embedding reason in metric name.
ops-bot: deploy notice: canary of telemetry v2 scheduled for 2026-04-01 02:00 UTC.
marta: plan proposal: 1) define public error enum (quota_burst, quota_reserved, transient_error, route_unavailable) 2) add header `X-Redwood-Error: <public_code>` + optional `X-Redwood-Retry-After` 3) emit telemetry metric `rw.client.error` with tag `public_code` and `route` 4) SDKs parse structured error object when available 5) console shows split-by public_code and mitigation cards. 6) rollout via feature flag + canary on 10% traffic.
ken: timeline ok. I'll draft RFC and mock console cards. we should also add a short-runbook for oncall: how to read new codes vs old 429 flood.
sasha: can we also include a subtle UX hint in the response body for web clients? e.g., `{ "error": "quota_burst", "message": "Traffic surge — retry in 30s or contact sales to increase throughput", "retry_after": 30 }` keep it small.
devon: yes keep body opt-in via `Accept: application/json` to avoid breaking text-only clients.
priya: will add dashboard mock and link to product playbook.
marta: thanks — I'll spin up the RFC and assign owners. tagging @ken to lead, @devon for SDKs, @priya for console, @sasha for infra telemetry. We'll use canary + gradual rollout, and deprecate ambiguous 429s in docs with a deprecation timeline. :thumbsup:
